prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single “best” company for everyone — the right choice depends on your exact location, roof type, budget, and whether you need an insurance-related replacement. I can find and vet top Miami contractors for you, but first here are the most important things to look for and a quick next step.

What to require from any Miami contractor doing hurricane-rated roof replacement
- Valid Florida license and registration — verify on the Florida DBPR site.  
- Miami‑Dade County high‑velocity hurricane zone (HVHZ) experience and familiarity with local code.  
- Use of Miami‑Dade or Florida Product Approval (NOA)‑listed materials and components. Ask for the NOA numbers.  
- Manufacturer‑approved installer status for the chosen system (shingles, metal, tile, TPO, etc.).  
- Written, itemized estimate with materials, fastening pattern, flashing details, underlayment, disposal and permit costs.  
- Clear, written warranty: both manufacturer warranty and a workmanship warranty from the contractor (length and transferability).  
- Proof of general liability insurance and workers’ comp.  
- References and photos of recent hurricane‑rated roofs in Miami (ideally within the last 2–3 years).  
- Will pull permits and pass inspections — verify permit history at the Miami‑Dade permit office if possible.

Questions to ask each contractor
- “Are you certified to install X product and can you provide the NOA numbers for the components?”  
- “How will you fasten the underlayment and shingles/tiles in HVHZ (nail pattern, adhesive, etc.)?”  
- “Who handles permits and inspections?”  
- “Can I see three recent Miami references and photos?”  
- “What’s the full warranty and what does it cover?”  
- “How do you handle storm‑damage insurance claims if applicable?”

Where to find and verify highly rated Miami roofers
- Florida DBPR license search (to confirm license status)  
- Miami‑Dade County permit records and NOA listings (for product approval)  
- BBB, Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi — read recent reviews and look for complaint resolution  
- Ask your insurance agent for contractors they’ve worked with on hurricane‑rated jobs

Material & design tips for hurricane resistance
- HIP roof shapes and properly tied rafters are stronger than unsupported gables.  
- Standing‑seam metal, properly anchored concrete/metal tile, and high‑wind rated shingles (installed to HVHZ specs) are common choices.  
- For low‑slope roofs, fully‑adhered TPO/EPDM or modified bitumen systems designed for HVHZ.  
- Flashings, roof‑to‑wall connections, and soffits/fascia must be upgraded — these are frequent failure points.

If you’d like, I can:
- Research and provide a short, vetted list of top hurricane‑rated roofers in Miami (with license verification, links to NOAs, reviews and contact info). If so, tell me your zip code or address (or the neighborhood) and whether you have a preferred material (metal, tile, shingle, TPO) or working with insurance.

Which option do you want?
